Baseline solver evidence: Candidate generation uses provided TrainOccupancyWindow values; API selects defaults or custom trains (backend/app/main.py:_trains_for; backend/app/solver_engine.py:_candidate_starts).
CP-SAT evidence: Shares baseline input normalization and candidate filter (backend/app/cpsat_solver.py:_normalise_inputs and _candidate_starts).
Operational gap / risk: No proof that supplied/listed trains are complete, current, or authoritative. Missing trains can create candidate time that appears free.
Required closure evidence: Authenticated provider record bound to route, date/time range, line/section, version and freshness; forged, missing, stale and partial evidence tests.

Baseline solver evidence: Filters candidate starts that overlap listed train windows on the same section and line (backend/app/solver_engine.py:_candidate_starts).
CP-SAT evidence: Uses the same candidate-start filtering (backend/app/cpsat_solver.py candidate construction).
Operational gap / risk: An optimizer's successful assignment only avoids listed intervals; it does not prove that no unlisted train occupies the worksite.
Required closure evidence: Approved occupancy semantics plus independent validator using complete authoritative intervals; endpoint and boundary tests.

Baseline solver evidence: Consumes section-level train intervals; no trajectory model in solver.
CP-SAT evidence: Consumes same section-level intervals; no trajectory model in CP-SAT.
Operational gap / risk: Data engine estimates section interval from route endpoints with linear position interpolation; this is not signaling/dispatch telemetry or verified physical position.
Required closure evidence: Documented data provenance/accuracy, route mapping validation and approved conservative uncertainty handling.

Requirement area: Operating date, service day, and time zone
Baseline solver evidence: Work orders and train windows use hour-of-day intervals; no date/service-day field in solver inputs.
CP-SAT evidence: Integer time variables are derived from the same hour-based inputs.
Operational gap / risk: Cross-day, date-specific service, daylight/time-zone rules, and timetable exceptions cannot be validated; data engine does not consume days_of_week.
Required closure evidence: Add validated date/time-zone/service calendar inputs and boundary tests, or declare the unsupported horizon explicitly.

Baseline solver evidence: Conflicts are checked by section and line in normalization/compatibility helpers.
CP-SAT evidence: Intervals grouped by section/line/department and compatibility checks reuse baseline helpers.
Operational gap / risk: Identifiers do not themselves establish possession limits, track topology, physical adjacency, or safe worksite boundaries.
Required closure evidence: Domain-owned track topology and possession mapping with input validation.

Current status: Modeled within same section and line
Baseline solver evidence: `_compatible` rejects overlapping same-section/same-line work except exact permitted cross-department co-location.
CP-SAT evidence: NoOverlap applies per section/line/department; pairwise rules handle cross-department overlap.
Operational gap / risk: No validated worksite geometry, access boundaries, setup/clearance margins, or physical protection model.
Required closure evidence: Approved overlap and clearance policy; tests at exact boundaries and with realistic worksite geometry.

Baseline solver evidence: Different track lines are compatible in baseline `_compatible`.
CP-SAT evidence: CP-SAT reuses this compatibility; no cross-line maintenance exclusion is added.
Operational gap / risk: Heavy equipment or access might foul the adjacent line, but neither optimizer checks maintenance-vs-maintenance across lines.
Required closure evidence: Operations/safety owner decision and explicit topology/equipment envelope constraints with tests.

Requirement area: Heavy equipment versus train on adjacent line
Baseline solver evidence: Candidate generation filters overlapping adjacent-line listed train windows for heavy work.
CP-SAT evidence: Same shared candidate filter; CP-SAT does not model a geometric envelope.
Operational gap / risk: A blanket temporal block may over-restrict; it also cannot establish completeness or distance from actual train position.
Required closure evidence: Approved physical clearance/equipment-envelope model and authenticated adjacent-line coverage.

Requirement area: Spatial buffer for concurrent same-line exposure
Baseline solver evidence: Optimizer does not model 1 km / 2 km spatial checks; solver assignment does not supply worksite km endpoints.
CP-SAT evidence: Optimizer does not model verifier spatial buffers.
Operational gap / risk: Safety verifier can return unknown for missing/malformed geometry. Solver completion is not spatial-clearance proof.
Required closure evidence: Trusted, validated chainage/worksite interval and route topology; test threshold equality and malformed/missing values.

Baseline solver evidence: Solver uses temporal filtering against trains, not geometric buffer against maintenance sites.
CP-SAT evidence: Shares temporal filter; no geometric distance decision variable.
Operational gap / risk: Verifier applies 1 km checks to adjacent-line train exposure, but has no authenticated timetable completeness or solver worksite geometry by default.
Required closure evidence: Authenticated coverage and geometry plus approved threshold/equipment-envelope validation.

Baseline solver evidence: No isolation constraints in solver. API clears solver-supplied positive claims before verification (backend/app/main.py:generate_schedule).
CP-SAT evidence: No isolation constraints; CP-SAT output is not evidence and is not used by the API.
Operational gap / risk: Positive Boolean/source label cannot prove electrical state; required traction checks remain unknown absent evidence.
Required closure evidence: Independent authenticated isolation provider tied to circuit, worksite, interval, authority and validity; adversarial API tests.

Current status: Not supplied as proof by API
Baseline solver evidence: Solver field is removed before verifier; baseline does not provide an independently validated proof.
CP-SAT evidence: CP-SAT does not establish FOL/safety proof; no production API path invokes it.
Operational gap / risk: A solver outcome or `fol_verified=True` must not bypass audit evidence. Current fail-closed behavior should be preserved.
Required closure evidence: Keep verifier independent and verify all applicable checks; test forged request/solver FOL flags.

Baseline solver evidence: No crew resource/calendar or capacity in MaintenanceWorkOrder/SolverRequest.
CP-SAT evidence: No crew variables/cumulative resource constraints.
Operational gap / risk: Concurrent tasks may require the same unavailable crew or exceed available staffing.
Required closure evidence: Approved crew data contract and cumulative resource constraints, with overload and boundary tests.

Baseline solver evidence: Department is not a credential/qualification model.
CP-SAT evidence: No skill/certification variables or eligibility constraints.
Operational gap / risk: No evidence that a qualified/authorized team is available for each work type.
Required closure evidence: Validated crew qualifications and task eligibility mapping; negative and missing-credential tests.

Current status: Not modeled; partial heavy-equipment flag only
Baseline solver evidence: `heavy_equipment` changes train conflict handling, but no inventory/capacity/type constraints.
CP-SAT evidence: Same inherited boolean usage; no equipment inventory/cumulative capacity.
Operational gap / risk: Equipment cannot be double-booked or matched to task requirements by either solver.
Required closure evidence: Equipment type/capacity/calendar contract and tested resource scheduling constraints.

Baseline solver evidence: No travel/setup/crew rest constraints; shift bins are objective accounting only.
CP-SAT evidence: No travel/setup/crew rest constraints.
Operational gap / risk: A schedule can be time-conflict-free but not executable by teams or equipment.
Required closure evidence: Domain specification, validated location/transition data, and resource-time constraints.

Baseline solver evidence: One duration field, contiguous interval; schema restricts positive duration up to 8 hours.
CP-SAT evidence: Optional interval uses fixed duration; CP-SAT time precision/scaling is additional.
Operational gap / risk: No uncertainty, phase durations, setup/clearance padding, or split-task semantics.
Required closure evidence: Approved duration source, buffers, precision, and tests for duration boundaries.

Baseline solver evidence: No per-order earliest start, latest finish, possession window, or deadline.
CP-SAT evidence: No such fields/constraints in CP-SAT model.
Operational gap / risk: Can schedule outside actual approved windows or after operational deadlines.
Required closure evidence: Add authoritative windows/deadlines only after source and semantics are approved; test infeasible windows.

Baseline solver evidence: No dependency/precedence graph.
CP-SAT evidence: No dependency/precedence variables or constraints.
Operational gap / risk: Related jobs can be scheduled in invalid sequence.
Required closure evidence: Add explicit dependency contract, cycle validation and precedence tests.

Baseline solver evidence: `defect_type` is descriptive; constraints use section, line, department, and co-location flag.
CP-SAT evidence: Same basic compatibility rules.
Operational gap / risk: No permit, method statement, access, possession, electrical, or task-specific requirements.
Required closure evidence: Approved task taxonomy and rules mapped to validated required evidence and hard constraints.

Baseline solver evidence: Urgency affects variable/value ordering and heuristic; no explicit weighted objective guarantee.
CP-SAT evidence: Urgency affects decision order, not coverage/secondary optimization objective.
Operational gap / risk: Higher urgency is not guaranteed to be scheduled first or preferred in a complete schedule.
Required closure evidence: Operations-approved priority semantics and objective/constraint tests.

Baseline solver evidence: Cross-department overlap allowed only for exact same section/line/window when both allow it; objective rewards merges.
CP-SAT evidence: Same compatibility rule; integer objective rewards merges.
Operational gap / risk: No shared-access or joint-worksite proof; exact equal times are a simplification.
Required closure evidence: Validate co-location eligibility, physical site, shared possession, and interaction with resources.

Baseline solver evidence: Complete assignment search; after exhaustion greedy partial fallback can leave work out. `solver_outcome=unschedulable` can coexist with `status=partial`.
CP-SAT evidence: Two-stage model maximizes coverage then optimizes secondary score; reports partial when maximum coverage is incomplete.
Operational gap / risk: Returned partial counts may match while selected orders/outcomes differ. Global infeasibility does not identify an individually impossible order.
Required closure evidence: Define one API contract and prove ID accounting; distinguish complete infeasibility, maximum-coverage partial, and capped unknown.

Baseline solver evidence: Backtracking reports whether complete search exhausted or hit node limit; baseline objective search does not certify global optimality.
CP-SAT evidence: CP-SAT exposes feasible/optimal/infeasible/unknown termination from solver status, subject to configured limit.
Operational gap / risk: A feasible incumbent is not an optimality proof; baseline has no global objective certificate. Outcome labels must not collapse these states.
Required closure evidence: Tests for each termination state; preserve proof fields and never infer infeasibility from timeout/cap.

Baseline solver evidence: Disruption, workload imbalance, and co-location terms used in baseline objective; simulated annealing can alter a solution.
CP-SAT evidence: Coverage is maximized first, then integer-scaled secondary objective; scaling/rounding can differ; no simulated annealing.
Operational gap / risk: Coverage lexicographic priority and precision can change selected schedules; baseline has no proven objective optimum for paired comparison.
Required closure evidence: Approve objective priority/weights/precision; independent objective evaluator and exhaustive small-instance comparisons.

Current status: Not established for CP-SAT production path
Baseline solver evidence: Production API invokes baseline and separately invokes safety verifier; no general independent hard-constraint validator is shown for solver output.
CP-SAT evidence: Experimental module only; production API does not invoke CP-SAT.
Operational gap / risk: The verifier is not a complete validator for every solver/resource constraint and does not prove data completeness.
Required closure evidence: Independent validator for all approved hard constraints before response; API tests against deliberately invalid solver output.

Current status: Conservative default, dependent on real evidence integration
Baseline solver evidence: API removes solver claims, verifies schedule, gives known failure precedence, and returns unverified for missing required evidence.
CP-SAT evidence: Not integrated into API; no evidence path from CP-SAT to production response.
Operational gap / risk: Current default blocks verified success but does not make schedule operationally safe; future wiring could create a trust bypass if careless.
Required closure evidence: Authenticated evidence gate, audit consistency checks, API regression suite, and no success on empty/incomplete audit.

Current status: Types exist; key fields not rendered
Baseline solver evidence: UI displays response status and counts; not solver outcome or unscheduled IDs.
CP-SAT evidence: CP-SAT outcome/proof is not integrated or presented.
Operational gap / risk: Users may not distinguish partial/limit/infeasible solver outcome from safety verification or see omitted work IDs.
Required closure evidence: Separate solver/safety badges, explicit unknown compliance, IDs, truthful reason text, and status-matrix UI tests.

Baseline solver evidence: Benchmark uses work orders from deterministic project generator and same train windows across seeds.
CP-SAT evidence: Same instances and inputs as baseline for paired runs.
Operational gap / risk: 10/25/50 only; 100/200 unsupported by 90 generated work orders. Different seeds are not different operational timetable scenarios.
Required closure evidence: Governed representative data and a documented distribution; do not extrapolate synthetic results.

Baseline solver evidence: 30 baseline rows, all complete, but objective proof unavailable; cap hits recorded for most 25/50 runs.
CP-SAT evidence: 120 paired rows, all complete and maximum coverage proved; objective optimality degrades with size/limit.
Operational gap / risk: No objective-quality comparison is interpretable against an unproven baseline optimum; no production performance conclusion.
Required closure evidence: Preserve per-run evidence, paired digests, proof-aware comparisons and independent governed benchmark.

Baseline solver evidence: Two partial cases have status=partial and outcome=unschedulable.
CP-SAT evidence: The same two cases have status=partial and outcome=partial.
Operational gap / risk: Preserved CSV marks both rows classification=equivalent despite same_solver_outcome=False; the report prose warns that outcomes differ. CSV-only consumers may miss the discrepancy.
Required closure evidence: Keep the preserved results immutable; future report generation must classify outcome mismatches explicitly and test classification against status/outcome columns.
